decision_reason: A1 gives weak seen support for climbing stairs and frontal elevation of arms, and walking is close to climbing stairs among unseen classes. Its global rotational_motion concept also conflates trunk bending, arm elevation, lower-limb cycling and crouching despite body-region-resolved IMU coverage. Splitting angular motion by body region, adding gravity-axis body translation and translation reversal, and dropping the constant motion_regularity dimension creates transferable contrasts without relying on recordings or sample statistics.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: axial_angular_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion of the chest and trunk segment, distinct from angular motion localized to the limbs.

levels.Low: Little or no chest or trunk angular motion.
levels.Medium: Moderate chest or trunk angular motion.
levels.High: Prominent chest or trunk angular motion.

attributes.name: upper_limb_angular_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion of the upper limb relative to the trunk and global load-bearing posture.

levels.Low: Little or no upper-limb angular motion.

attributes.name: lower_limb_angular_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion of the lower limb associated with stepping, pedaling, crouching or other leg articulation.

levels.Low: Little or no lower-limb angular motion.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: vertical_body_translation
attributes.definition: Prominence of translation of the global load-bearing body along the gravity direction, including repeated ascent, descent or vertical excursion.

levels.Low: Little or no gravity-axis translation of the load-bearing body.
levels.Medium: Moderate gravity-axis translation or vertical excursion.
levels.High: Prominent repeated or sustained gravity-axis translation.

attributes.name: translation_reversal
attributes.definition: Degree to which locomotor translation repeatedly reverses direction rather than maintaining progression in a consistent direction.

levels.Low: Little or no repeated reversal of translational direction.
levels.Medium: Occasional or moderately expressed translational reversals.
levels.High: Clear and repeated alternation of translational direction.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains a supported transferable distinction between moderate walking or arm motion and vigorous stair climbing or jumping, with jogging and running providing seen high-intensity anchors.
Repetition rate is physically distinct from motion energy and transfers from cycling, jogging and running to periodic unseen locomotion and arm repetitions.
Sustained rapid fluctuation remains independent of isolated impacts and helps contrast smooth arm elevation with abrupt jumping, using waist bending and running as seen anchors.
Short high-magnitude impacts are directly relevant to jump landings and distinguish them from smooth non-impact arm elevation and bending; running supplies a seen high-impact anchor.

Mean gravity-relative load-bearing posture remains useful for separating upright walking or arm elevation from the more inclined configuration associated with stair climbing, with static postures and cycling providing seen anchors.
Changes in global load-bearing orientation distinguish whole-body postural modulation in stair climbing or jumping from local arm elevation, and transfer from waist bending and crouching.

The global A1 concept assigns prominent rotation to physically different trunk, arm and leg actions. Body-region-resolved angular semantics add a supported contrast between frontal elevation of arms and its nearest seen waist-bending anchor while retaining transferable lower-limb distinctions from cycling and crouching.
Overall sustained locomotor progression remains necessary to separate walking and stair climbing from local arm or trunk exercises, with jogging, running and cycling as seen translation anchors.
Every supplied A1 class prototype has High motion_regularity, so the concept contributes no split-specific class contrast despite being measurable in principle.

Gravity-axis body translation adds an independent and physically supported distinction for the low-U_NN walking versus climbing stairs pair. Crouching supplies a seen anchor for substantial vertical body excursion, while jogging and running anchor locomotor vertical dynamics.

Repeated front-back direction reversal separates jump front & back from the sustained progression of walking, stair climbing, jogging and running without duplicating impact magnitude or overall translation.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final concepts are complementary rather than interchangeable. Motion_intensity measures total energy, smoothness measures sustained rapid fluctuation, and impulsiveness measures isolated abrupt peaks. Cadence measures repetition rate rather than regularity or intensity. Posture_inclination measures mean global orientation, posture_variability measures its temporal change, and axial_angular_motion measures trunk angular-motion prominence. Upper_limb_angular_motion and lower_limb_angular_motion localize articulation to different body regions. Translational_motion measures overall sustained progression, vertical_body_translation isolates its gravity-axis component or excursion, and translation_reversal measures repeated directional alternation. The non-discriminative A1 motion_regularity coordinate is removed.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
